messages:
lina: Heads-up — noticed a short ECC/Xid burst hitting the us-west-2 GPU pool around 12:02 PT. ~6 cards showed transient ECC counts over ~90s, DCGM exporter spiked and alerts fired then cleared. Opening a thread to propose an adaptive hysteresis + recording-rule approach to cut noisy drains.

ops-bot: Alert: dcgm_ecc_errors_total spike on p-tasks-gpu-usw2 at 2026-03-17T19:02:03Z (auto-note)

mike: Saw that. I checked node logs — there were driver reset entries on 3 nodes within the same minute, others look like single-bump ECC counters. No pod restarts or OOMs. Pattern looks like longer runtimes (>=48h) precede the bursts.

sam: Current prom rule is effectively `dcgm_ecc_errors_total > 0 for 1m -> page`. Way too noisy for fleet ops.

jen: Agree. My quick proposal: compute a short-term rate (burst counter) and gate alerts on both sustained rate and cardinality (distinct cards). Add hysteresis so we don't immediately drain on a 1-off flake. Also backoff to avoid repeated drain attempts on same node.

lina: I sketched a couple of recording rules and an alert expr — rough POC below, want quick feedback: 
```yaml
# recording rule: per-minute ECC increase (short window)
record: dcgm:ecc_rate_per_min:increase
expr: increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[1m])
# also record a distinct-card count by node over 3m
record: dcgm:ecc_distinct_cards_3m:sum
expr: count_values("gpu_uuid", increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[3m])) by (node)
```
Alert suggestion:
```yaml
alert: GPU_ECC_BURST
expr: sum by (node)(dcgm:ecc_rate_per_min:increase) > 3 and dcgm:ecc_distinct_cards_3m:sum > 2
for: 3m
labels: {severity: warning}
annotations: {runbook: 'https://go.redwood/gpu-ecc-playbook'}
```
This should only fire on short sustained bursts affecting multiple cards on the same node.

mike: Looks reasonable. A couple of notes: normalize labels (e.g., `gpu_model`/`gpu_pci_id`) so we can exclude known noisy SKUs. Also consider using `changes()` on `gpu_driver_restarts_total` to suppress alerts when a driver restart is detected.

jen: +1. We should add an inhibition rule in Alertmanager: if `gpu_driver_restarts_total` increased in last 5m, inhibit the ECC burst alert for that node to avoid double-triage. Also add a lower-severity route that doesn't auto-drain — route to ops channel first.

sam: Can we make it adaptive? Example: scale the threshold by cluster utilization or active work per node. If utilization is low, be more lenient; if we're at high SLO load, be stricter and trigger fallback routing instead of immediate drain. Might be a knob in the rollout config (hosted vs dedicated).

lina: Good idea — we can add a `node_load_factor` label from our exporter and use it to scale `> 3` threshold (e.g., `> ceil(3 * node_load_factor)`). I'll prototype that. I'll also include an annotation with `no_auto_drain: true` by default and flip it for high-criticality customers.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: opened PR https://git.redwood/infrastructure/monitoring/pulls/87 with initial recording rules + alert + playbook link

jen: Thanks — I'll review the PR tomorrow. Also add `gpu_pci_id` tags so we can add a suppress list for historically flaky models.

lina: Great — assigning to myself to push the POC, will ping for reviews @jen @mike. Planning to run the rule in evaluation mode (recording only + noisy logging) for 48h before flip. :thumbsup:
